report.overall: WETH9 implements a minimal wrapped Ether contract with payable deposit, withdraw using balance checks and transfer, and ERC20-style transfers/approvals. No high or medium Slither findings are present. The code follows checks-effects-interactions in withdraw and emits all relevant events.

checklist.note: No owner or privileged functions present in source.
No proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade logic in WETH9.sol.
withdraw updates balanceOf before msg.sender.transfer.
No oracles or price feeds referenced in code.
Uses require on balance before -= and direct += on deposit.
Only msg.sender.transfer after state update; no other external calls.
No signatures or EIP-712 logic in source.
No pause or emergency stop functions defined.
approve sets allowance; transferFrom checks allowance != uint(-1) and deducts.
Deposit, Withdrawal, Approval, Transfer events emitted on all state changes.

report.overall: TetherToken implements a deprecated upgrade path, owner-controlled pausing/blacklisting/fee params, and custom transfer logic with SafeMath. All 15 Slither Medium findings are erc20-interface mismatches stemming from the 0.4-era interface declarations versus the actual function bodies that add onlyPayloadSize, fees, and deprecation forwarding. No other high-severity issues are indicated by the provided tool output.

checklist.note: onlyOwner used on issue/redeem/deprecate/setParams/pause; owner set in constructor and transferable.
deprecated flag forwards selected calls to arbitrary upgradedAddress; no access control on the proxy target itself.
No external calls before state updates; only internal balance adjustments and events.
No oracles or price feeds present in the contract.
SafeMath used for all arithmetic; onlyPayloadSize also present.
Calls to upgradedAddress when deprecated; target is fully trusted by owner only.
No signatures or EIP-712 logic in the source.
Pausable with whenNotPaused on transfers; owner-only pause/unpause.
Standard approve with zero-value race-condition guard; forwarded when deprecated.
Transfer/Approval/Issue/Redeem/Deprecate/Params/BlackList events emitted on state changes.

slither_triage.why: All 15 reports cite interface mismatches on transfer/transferFrom/approve; these are intentional because the functions add onlyPayloadSize, fee logic, blacklist checks, and deprecation forwarding that the base ERC20/ERC20Basic declarations omit.

No external calls visible in FiatTokenV2_2 functions; all state changes are internal.

_setBalance enforces _balance <= ((1 << 255) - 1) and _isBlacklisted check; _balanceOf uses bitmask.
No external calls in the provided FiatTokenV2_2 code.
permit, transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization accept signature bytes and delegate to internal _ functions with nonce/deadline parameters.

No event emissions visible in the FiatTokenV2_2 source functions.

slither_triage.why: No High/Medium reported; counts align with common patterns in storage packing (_balanceOf/_setBalance) and override methods without unsafe external calls.

report.overall: UniswapV2Factory.sol implements UniswapV2Factory with createPair using create2 and access restricted to feeToSetter for setFeeTo/setFeeToSetter; UniswapV2Pair uses a lock modifier and performs external token calls plus optional callee callbacks. Slither reports one High (weak-prng on block.timestamp) and five Medium findings on equality checks and reentrancy-no-eth in swap/burn/createPair/mint paths, all directly matching the provided source lines. No upgrade, pause, or signature logic exists in the contracts.

checklist.note: setFeeTo and setFeeToSetter require msg.sender == feeToSetter; initialize requires msg.sender == factory; createPair enforces token ordering and zero-address checks.
No proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade mechanisms present in UniswapV2Factory, UniswapV2Pair or UniswapV2ERC20.
lock modifier used on mint/burn/swap/skim/sync; however reentrancy-no-eth flagged after _safeTransfer and IUniswapV2Callee calls before state writes in swap, burn and createPair.
_update computes price0CumulativeLast/price1CumulativeLast using UQ112x112 from reserves; no external oracle calls.
SafeMath used for add/sub/mul; Math.sqrt and UQ112x112.encode/uqdiv used for liquidity and prices; require checks prevent overflow in _update.
_safeTransfer performs token.call(SELECTOR) and swap may call IUniswapV2Callee.uniswapV2Call; reentrancy flags on post-call state updates.
permit uses EIP-712 with DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, nonces increment, deadline check and ecrecover; no other signature logic.
No pause, emergency stop or circuit-breaker functions defined.
transferFrom respects allowance == uint(-1) sentinel; _approve and allowance mappings standard.
PairCreated, Mint, Burn, Swap, Sync and Approval/Transfer events emitted at required points.

slither_triage.why: blockTimestamp = uint32(block.timestamp % 2**32) in _update matches code at line 266 and is used only for timeElapsed in price accumulators.
data.length == 0 check in _safeTransfer (line 237) and _totalSupply == 0 in mint (line 310) are standard patterns for optional return value and first-mint liquidity.
Flags in swap (350), burn (325) and createPair (411) after external calls before state writes; lock modifier present but cross-function getPair writes noted.

report.overall: UniswapV2Router02 is a non-upgradeable contract with immutable factory and WETH addresses set only in the constructor. Slither reports 3 high-severity issues (reentrancy-balance in two fee-on-transfer swap functions and one unchecked-transfer in removeLiquidity) plus 6 medium unused-return findings, all directly matching the provided source. No access-control, pausing, or event emission logic exists beyond the ensure deadline modifier.

checklist.note: No owner or privileged roles; all external functions are callable by anyone and use only the ensure(deadline) modifier present in the code.
Constructor sets immutable factory and WETH; no proxy or upgrade logic in the source.

Reentrancy-balance flagged by Slither in swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens and swapExactETHForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens via _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens calling pair.swap.
No external price oracles; only internal UniswapV2Library.getReserves and quote calls appear in the code.
Uses SafeMath for uint; no unchecked arithmetic visible in provided functions.
Multiple external calls to pairs, factory, and tokens without reentrancy guards in the fee-on-transfer paths listed by Slither.
No signature verification or permit logic implemented inside this router; only forwards to pair.permit in removeLiquidityWithPermit.
No pause or emergency-stop functions present in the source.
removeLiquidity performs IUniswapV2Pair(pair).transferFrom without checking its return value, matching the unchecked-transfer finding.
No events are emitted by any function in the provided source code.

slither_triage.why: Matches the two swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens functions that read balanceBefore before the external pair.swap call.
Directly matches IUniswapV2Pair(pair).transferFrom return value ignored in removeLiquidity at line 328.
All six instances are ignored return values from sortTokens, getReserves, and createPair that the router does not need.

report.overall: SwapRouter (contracts/SwapRouter.sol) is a stateless router that executes exactInput/exactOutput swaps via pool.swap callbacks and inherits Multicall, PeripheryPaymentsWithFee, SelfPermit and PeripheryValidation. All high-impact Slither findings originate in the inherited base contracts (Multicall, PeripheryPayments) rather than SwapRouter itself; the supplied source contains no access-control, upgrade, oracle or pause logic. The contract relies on msg.sender as payer, block.timestamp deadlines and delegatecall for multicall, with token transfers performed only through verified callbacks.

checklist.note: No owner, role or access-control modifiers present in SwapRouter or its listed bases.
Contract has no proxy, implementation or upgrade logic; constructor only sets immutable factory and WETH9.
Multicall.multicall performs delegatecall in a payable loop; exactInput loops call external pool.swap which triggers uniswapV3SwapCallback.
No price oracles; swaps use direct IUniswapV3Pool.swap with TickMath bounds or caller-supplied sqrtPriceLimitX96.
Uses SafeCast.toInt256 and explicit amount0/amount1 sign checks; no unchecked arithmetic visible in supplied SwapRouter or Path/BytesLib.
Calls getPool(...).swap, pay (inherited), IWETH9 and arbitrary ERC20 via TransferHelper; CallbackValidation.verifyCallback only checks pool existence.
SelfPermit wraps IERC20Permit.permit and IERC20PermitAllowed.permit with msg.sender as owner; deadlines and nonces handled by token contracts.
No pause, circuit-breaker or emergency-stop functions in any supplied file.
pay uses arbitrary payer in safeTransferFrom; SelfPermitIfNecessary checks allowance before calling permit.
No events emitted in SwapRouter, Multicall, Path, SelfPermit or PeripheryValidation.

slither_triage.why: pay is intentionally called with data.payer (msg.sender or address(this)) after CallbackValidation; pattern is required for router to move user funds.
Multicall.multicall is the documented multicall entrypoint; results are collected and reverts bubble up, matching intended behavior.
Finding points to FullMath in @uniswap/v3-core which is not part of the supplied SwapRouter source.
PeripheryPayments.pay ignores WETH9.transfer return value; code path reachable via exactInputSingle when recipient is router.

report.overall: Permit2 (src/Permit2.sol) is an empty unification contract inheriting SignatureTransfer and AllowanceTransfer with no additional logic. All transfer paths rely on prior ERC20 approvals to Permit2 and EIP-712 signatures verified via SignatureVerification; no access control, upgradeability, pausing, oracles, or arithmetic beyond uint160/uint48 packing appear in the provided sources. Slither high findings on arbitrary-send-erc20 are expected for a transfer-permit contract while the uninitialized-local reports are artifacts of conditional EOA vs. ERC1271 paths.

checklist.note: No owner or privileged roles; all state changes gated by msg.sender allowances or owner signatures in permit/transferFrom.
No proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade logic present in Permit2, EIP712, AllowanceTransfer, SignatureTransfer or libraries.
External calls limited to safeTransferFrom and IERC1271.isValidSignature after nonce/signature checks; no reentrant state writes observed.
No price feeds, oracles, or external data sources referenced in any provided file.
Only unchecked decrement of allowance.amount and nonce packing; no multiplication/division that could overflow.
ERC20.safeTransferFrom and IERC1271.isValidSignature called on arbitrary token/claimedSigner addresses supplied by callers.
EIP712 domain separator caches chainId; nonces invalidated via bitmap or sequential nonce in Allowance; SignatureExpired checks present.
No pause flag, emergency withdrawal, or circuit-breaker functions defined.
Users must approve Permit2; contract only reads/writes PackedAllowance and calls safeTransferFrom after validation.
Approval, Permit, Lockdown, NonceInvalidation, and UnorderedNonceInvalidation events emitted on state changes.

slither_triage.why: AllowanceTransfer._transfer and SignatureTransfer._permitTransferFrom intentionally call safeTransferFrom(from,...) where from is the permit owner or allowance holder.
r,s,v declared at top of SignatureVerification.verify but assigned only in the EOA branch; contract-signer branch never reads them.

report.overall: UNI token implements ERC20 with delegation checkpoints, controlled minting via time-gated minter, and EIP-2612 permits. The reported medium finding is the only flagged issue and matches the checkpoint logic present in the source. All other categories show standard patterns with no high-severity problems.

checklist.note: minter role enforced in constructor, setMinter, and mint; only minter can change itself or mint after mintingAllowedAfter
no proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade logic present in Uni.sol

nonces incremented in permit and delegateBySig; DOMAIN_TYPEHASH and typehashes match EIP-712
no pause or emergency-stop mechanism implemented

report.overall: LinkToken implements ERC20 with ERC677 extensions, minting totalSupply in constructor and using SafeMath for all balance updates. The single medium Slither finding reports totalSupply shadowing, which matches the constant declaration at line 222 versus the abstract at line 41.

checklist.note: Only constructor assigns balances[msg.sender]; no owner or privileged functions present in LinkToken, StandardToken, or ERC677Token.
No proxy, delegatecall, or upgrade logic in any contract; LinkToken is deployed as a standalone contract.

Transfer and Approval events emitted in BasicToken, StandardToken, and ERC677Token; Transfer with data emitted on transferAndCall.

slither_triage.why: LinkToken declares constant totalSupply at L222 to provide the ERC20Basic interface value; shadowing is the intended implementation pattern for this token contract.

report.overall: Lido.sol implements a complex liquid staking contract inheriting from AragonApp, StETHPermit and Versioned with extensive use of unstructured storage, role-based access control and oracle-driven accounting. The single High finding from Slither on _submit is contradicted by the payable fallback and submit functions that explicitly call it; the Medium findings are almost entirely assembly-based view functions in imported libraries. No reentrancy, arithmetic or signature issues are visible in the supplied source.

checklist.note: Uses _auth with PAUSE_ROLE, RESUME_ROLE, STAKING_PAUSE_ROLE, STAKING_CONTROL_ROLE and UNSAFE_CHANGE_DEPOSITED_VALIDATORS_ROLE; all privileged functions check roles before state changes.
Explicit finalizeUpgrade_v2 and _initialize_v2 paths; version checks via _checkContractVersion and setContractVersion.
No external calls inside value-transferring paths that could re-enter; receiveELRewards and receiveWithdrawals are restricted to locator addresses.
handleOracleReport path (truncated in source) relies on IOracleReportSanityChecker and external accounting oracle; uninitialized reportContext local flagged by Slither.
SafeMath used throughout; no raw overflow patterns visible in supplied Lido.sol code.
Calls to ILidoLocator, IStakingRouter, IWithdrawalQueue etc. are performed via interface; no unchecked low-level calls in the provided file.
StETHPermit inherited but no ECDSA or signature logic present inside Lido.sol itself.
pauseStaking, resumeStaking, stop and resume functions implemented with dedicated roles and events.
Infinite allowance set once in _initialize_v2 to burner from withdrawalQueue; uses internal _approve.
Emits StakingPaused, ETHDistributed, TokenRebased, Submitted, Unbuffered and locator events on all state changes.

slither_triage.why: _submit is called only from the payable fallback and payable submit function shown in source; internal function can receive value in 0.4.x.

All 13 instances are in @aragon/os and local libraries (UnstructuredStorage, IsContract, ECDSA, StakeLimitUtils, SignatureUtils, ConversionHelpers, SafeERC20) that legitimately use assembly for storage or gas-efficient reads.
depositsValue in deposit() and reportContext in _handleOracleReport are declared but never initialized in the provided source; may be assigned later in the truncated function body.

report.overall: Pool.sol delegates all core operations to external logic libraries and relies on PoolAddressesProvider for access control and oracle addresses. The contract itself implements onlyPoolConfigurator, onlyPoolAdmin and onlyBridge modifiers plus initializer-based upgradeability via VersionedInitializable. Slither reports are confined to the listed library files and do not reference any function body inside Pool.sol.

checklist.note: onlyPoolConfigurator, onlyPoolAdmin and onlyBridge modifiers are defined and used on all privileged entry points; they call ADDRESSES_PROVIDER.getPoolConfigurator and IACLManager.isPoolAdmin/isBridge.
Inherits VersionedInitializable; initialize is protected by initializer modifier and checks provider == ADDRESSES_PROVIDER; POOL_REVISION = 0x3.
No ReentrancyGuard or nonReentrant modifier appears in Pool.sol; all external calls are performed inside the delegated Logic libraries.
ADDRESSES_PROVIDER.getPriceOracle() and getPriceOracleSentinel() are passed to BorrowLogic, SupplyLogic, LiquidationLogic and PoolLogic.
No arithmetic operations are present in Pool.sol; all calculations reside in the imported Logic and Math libraries.
Pool performs external calls via the delegated libraries (e.g. IERC20WithPermit.permit, FlashLoanLogic.executeFlashLoan); the arbitrary-send-erc20 finding is reported in FlashLoanLogic.
supplyWithPermit and repayWithPermit call IERC20WithPermit.permit before executing the corresponding logic; deadline, v, r, s are forwarded.
No pause, unpause or emergency functions are declared in Pool.sol.
permit is used for supplyWithPermit and repayWithPermit; no direct approve calls exist in this file.
No event declarations or emit statements appear in the provided Pool.sol source.

slither_triage.why: Flash loan repayment intentionally transfers from the receiverAddress supplied by the caller; the pattern is required for the flash-loan feature.
IncentivizedERC20 is not part of the supplied Pool.sol; totalSupply is expected to be initialized by the aToken / debt token constructors outside this file.
MathUtils.calculateCompoundedInterest uses fixed-point ray math; the reported division is part of the standard compounded-interest approximation.

Strict timestamp equality checks (lastUpdateTimestamp == block.timestamp, exp == 0) are standard short-circuit guards in ReserveLogic and MathUtils to avoid unnecessary work when state is already up-to-date.
